title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — our corruption is ours by propagation; the begetting act not ours
pass_a_gloss: Placeus grants the spoil is ours once it lives inside us by generation. He refuses to treat the begetting deed as ours in the same way: it becomes ours only as that spoil is a share in it and a yes to it—not as a personal repeat of paradise.
pass_b_english: Certainly the corruption is ours, because propagated into us, it is within us; but the act which begot the corruption is not ours except insofar as the corruption is a certain participation of it, and there is consent unto it.
source_text: Certe corruptio nostra est, quia in nos propagata, intra nos est; actio vero quae corruptionem peperit non est nostra nisi quatenus corruptio eius quaedam participatio, & in eam consensio est.

choices.choice: Corruption ours by propagation; begetting act not personally ours
